#9075. Death Row’s Last Meals Anchor a Museum-Wide Survey of Incarceration Art

Louisiana State Penitentiary, known as “Angola” for the slave plantation that once occupied its land, lies at the dead end of Highway 66.

Past the gate, the road continues—invitation permitting—through 18,000 acres of penal farmland punctuated by gun towers, barbed-wire enclosures, and incarcerated men picking crops on the so-called farm line. America’s largest maximum-security prison, long notorious for its reliance on solitary confinement, Angola runs on the forgotten.

Gary Tyler, a fiber artist and activist, remembers Angola. He arrived in 1974 at seventeen years old, wrongly convicted of shooting a white student during a segregationist mob’s attack on his school bus. The prison is bound on three sides by bayou, bluffs, and swamp; escaping into one’s mind was easier. His grandmother was a quilter, he said, and fabric could be found or bartered. Time was given. Over four decades inside, including two stints on death row, he got good, even renowned. Craftswomen from across the South came to Angola to find the man behind the textiles making rounds outside. Related Articles Art en Route: Museum of London Eyes Trump Baby Balloon, Art Institute of Chicago Deaccessions Chinese Artworks, and More Other Voices, Other Worlds

“All that time, I never thought of myself as an ‘artist,’” Tyler said at the opening of “Rebirth,” a solo show of his quilted and appliquéd works at the Grand Rapids Art Museum. “I said, ‘Call me a hobbyist.’ Artists were people in galleries, people with an audience.”

“Rebirth” is one of three solo presentations on view in Grand Rapids through January 2027 that showcase art by or about people once incarcerated within the United States. Ray Materson, whose show is subtitled “Metamorphosis,” works in a medium he invented during his prison sentence for a drug-fueled robbery with a toy gun: palm-sized embroideries stitched by hand from the threads of unraveled socks, Americana meets Renaissance miniature.

The third show is The Last Supper, a 1,000-piece ceramic installation by the artist Julie Green, shown in its entirety for only the second time. For twenty years, up until their death in 2021, Green illustrated final-meal choices on ceramic plates painted in cobalt blue and re-fired in her kiln. What does the condemned order on death row? An overflowing bucket of Kentucky Fried Chicken, lobster, steak, burgers and fries, pecan pie. Nothing, sometimes: inmates can refuse or be denied a selection. (Final meal selections are generally a matter of public records.) At a quick glance, these plates might pass for Staffordshire. A closer look could ruin your lunch.

“It’s not so much that these shows are timely,” said Jennifer Wcisel, curator of collections at the Grand Rapids Art Museum. “It’s that the question of what incarceration means to American life is never absent. It’s ongoing.”

But has punishment been so openly advertised since the pre-Civil Rights era? Tennessee’s botched attempt to execute Christa Pike, the only woman on its death row, was followed by a magazine interview with the physician on hand to pronounce her dead (he said the state should try again). The Defense Secretary called for the military’s first execution in six decades—by firing squad—to be livestreamed. The White House launched an online arcade, where in one game a pixelated Border Patrol agent, rounds up “border crossers.”

The art can’t hope to match the volume of cruelty. It aspires to empathy or at least empathy’s catalyst: curiosity. Whose aim does a public execution serve? Within the carceral system, how is dignity doled out?

The Last Supper argues that dignity is a fickle allowance. Texas ended special last meals in 2011, after white supremacist Lawrence Russell Brewer ordered a feast and left it untouched. Set against Green’s terrible, tender plates, the result is hard to defend. Bite-size biographies like “he never had a birthday cake so we ordered a birth-day cake for him” give way to row upon row of “Standard prison fare.” This is dinnerware for a haunted house.

It is also a map of America’s patchwork principles on capital punishment. The Supreme Court barred executing people with intellectual disabilities in 2002, then left the states to define who qualifies, within limits. One plate records an IQ of 61, well below the benchmark of about 70, and a request that the menu not be released to the media. Another records a request that their meal be saved until after the execution.

Everything on view is portraiture, if the word can stretch to cover a spirit given a recognizable shape, even one abridged to a birthday cake. Tyler and Materson work with representational directness in the opposite register from Green. We see faces. Their work can indulge fantasy, the province of the living. One of Tyler’s quilts depicts a former inmate known as Big Toe in the so-called Greek Alps, still wearing the armor from The Life of Jesus Christ, a play produced by the drama club Tyler founded. Portraiture at its best is said to reveal the heart. For centuries it was also a privilege of the powerful, who commissioned likenesses to control how they were seen. Prison inverts that arrangement: the powerful do the watching. But what does surveillance ever capture of its subjects? Insight can’t be taken, only given.

Materson’s intricate embroideries stray in their subjects from baseball to outer space, with the most striking blending imagination and documentation. In Self-Portrait (undated), he sits before a mirror, stitching the very piece the viewer is looking at. Down a receding tunnel, a smaller Materson stitches a smaller Materson, and so on: infinity, or its likeness. The thick black frame that cages his face is made of the same thread as the rest, not impossibly undone.

One quilt late in Tyler’s show features a great crane, the kind that roosted in the wetlands around Angola and sometimes landed in the prison yard. Tyler was released in 2016, after decades of campaigning by activists including Rosa Parks. The crane captures that moment. His soul, he said, sprang skyward on his first step outside. It has yet to descend.

Tyler’s Convict Poker (2025) unfolds at the Angola prison rodeo: a Black man hangs in midair, bucked from a bull. The last of its kind in the country, the event is held twice a year and open to a paying public. Spectators can’t legally bet; the gamble belongs to the prisoners who volunteer. In convict poker, a raging bull is loosed on a mock card game, and the last man still seated wins a prize. Posting this October’s rodeo to Facebook, an attendee wrote: “The announcer said they didn’t run that fast from the PoPo 🚓😂 Watch til the end, prisoners were flying…”

Tyler never rode in the rodeo. But he doesn’t judge. (One of his quilts were raffled at the rodeo and raised $30,000 for the hospice program.) The men who volunteer, he said, are willing “to jeopardize their lives or go through a sense of degradation just to entertain an audience because nobody wants to be forgotten.”

“These are men who may never go home. The announcer mentions their names, and that they are serving life sentences; understand?”

#9074. Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home.

Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up!

Why are my ears clogged?

Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked:

  • Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage.
  • If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection.
  • Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side.
  • Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too.
  • Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure.

Best clogged ear remedies

1. Pop and unclog

The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes.

2. Swallow, yawn, or chew

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow.

3. Ear drops

Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes.

Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful.

4. Warmth and gravity

To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily.

5. Hit the steam room

Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 

6. Take allergy medication

Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears.

Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort.

7. Rinse away the gunk

Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing.

When to see your doctor

Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention.

What not to do when you have clogged ears

  • Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. 
  • Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries.
  • Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion.
  • Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation.

Takeaway

Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies.

PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

#9072. Solid cork forms walls of pavilion dedicated to silence at Casa No Tempo in Alentejo

Photography by Mercês Tomaz Gomes

Antwerp-based studio Corkinho has unveiled its latest “still room”, a pavilion with walls of solid cork, which is installed in the grounds of a vacation villa designed by Manuel Aires Mateus.

The still room is a space dedicated to silent and introspective activities, such as reading, yoga, tea ceremonies or meditation.

Corkinho installed it in the grounds of Casa No Tempo, a former farmhouse in southern Portugal, which architect Aires Mateus converted into a holiday home in 2014 for hospitality entrepreneur João Rodrigues.

Lead designer Cédric Etienne devised the building’s innovative structure, which is fully demountable, with the help of architect and master carpenter Gonçalo Madeira Marrote of Madeiguincho.

The floor slab is a timber deck, built over a foundation of removable concrete blocks.

Above this, solid blocks of cork are stacked up like giant bricks to form the building’s walls and secured with metal rods that thread through milled channels.

The pavilion is topped by a timber roof, described by Etienne as “like a hat with four screws”, which helps to weigh down the cork blocks.

“I wanted it to be zero waste and carbon-neutral,” the designer told Dezeen.

“If we need to dismantle it, we can place it somewhere else. There is no glue and no screws,” he said.

“It’s like the Japanese way of building teahouses, with total respect of the local materials and no harm to the land.”

As the name suggests, Corkinho is a studio that specialises in objects and spaces built from cork.

The studio first launched the still room concept in 2020, when it moved its office into the former Noorderpershuis power station in Antwerp and transformed one of the rooms into a silent sanctuary.

Etienne defines a still room as any space where you can pause your mind and be still.

“It’s a place where you disconnect from noise and distractions and invite a deeper sense of presence,” he said.

After consulting with various hotel brands keen to adopt the concept, Etienne pitched the idea to Rodrigues and his company, Silent Living.

The company has five properties, all designed by Aires Mateus and all with a focus on slow living.

“I had been to Casa No Tempo many times, so I knew the place like an inner home,” the designer said.

“It felt so aligned in terms of feeling and senses, so I thought it could be a really beautiful challenge to move the concept forward in this place,” he continued.

The room can be used by guests staying at the villa, but it can also accommodate curated programmes.

Etienne has been hosting four-day silent retreats, allowing groups of designers and hospitality professionals to learn more about the still room concept.

The cork blocks, supplied by locally based company Sofalca, were heat-treated to improve their durability. The material gives the building impressive sensorial and thermal qualities, Etienne said.

“All the technical properties of cork – the acoustics, the scent, the softness – all become architectural conditions,” he stated.

“You really feel like you’re coming into a womb. Even when it’s 40 degrees outside, the temperature inside is around 22 or 23.”

Other pavilions recently featured in Dezeen include a wildlife pavilion informed by rippling water and a jigsaw-like pavilion made of mass-timber scrap.

#9071. Are Tangerines Good for You? 5 Health Benefits You Might Love

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

#9069. Many London architecture firms not paying London Living Wage

The majority of the London-based studios in The Pay 100‘s fifth annual salary survey are not paying Part I architectural assistants the London Living Wage, as required by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA).

An engineering firm has topped the leaderboard for the average salaries for UK architects, according to a survey conducted by the anonymous group The Pay 100.

Engineering firm tops architect salary leaderboard

Published over the weekend, the survey provides rough figures only based on the mean figures submitted by respondents. This year’s data collected the annual salary of 127 firms in the UK and the mean number of hours of unpaid overtime per week.

Topping the leaderboard with the highest average annual salary for architects with less than five years’ experience is BakerHicks, an engineering and design firm, which paid £72,000, according to the survey.

Second on the list is London studio Hawkins\Brown at £63,700, and joint third at £56,300 are London practices Samuel Chisholm Studio and Thomas Alexander Design.

The survey also presented figures for Part I and Part II architectural assistants. Transport for London had the highest wage for Part II roles at £44,000, followed by Foster + Partners at £42,000.

Majority of London firms not paying London Living Wage

The results for Part I roles included salaries from 30 studios, 21 of which were based in Greater London.

Only the top four studios on the leaderboard – Haworth Tompkins, Allford Hall Monaghan Morris, Studio McW and Studio PDP – paid more than the London Living Wage of £32,136, which RIBA declared a requirement for relevant offices.

Twelve of the 30 studios were paying Part I roles less than the £29,328 UK Living Wage.

Low wages “a threat to the future of the profession”

Alongside its survey data, The Pay 100 wrote an open letter to RIBA, asking it to take action on the financial wellbeing of those working in the architecture industry and to ensure the long-term future of the profession.

“Our aim has always been to create tangible financial incentives for employers to improve pay, empower employees to make informed career decisions, and encourage a healthier, more sustainable profession,” said The Pay 100 in the letter.

“We recognise that architecture practices operate within a highly competitive market, often under significant financial pressure themselves,” it continued. “Nevertheless, the commercial challenges facing practices should not prevent the profession from addressing the deteriorating conditions experienced by many employees.”

“Poor financial conditions for staff are not merely an employment issue; they are a threat to the long-term health, resilience and future of the profession.”

It went on to set out two courses of action it called for RIBA to take: establishing “meaningful minimum salaries” for RIBA chartered practices, and taking full ownership of The Pay 100 and its annual salary survey.

The Pay 100 said a framework of minimum salary levels should be established across different architecture roles, increasing year-on-year in line with inflation.

“A profession cannot sustainably advocate for the value of its services while leaving the financial conditions of its workforce to market pressures alone,” it said. “The RIBA should take a leading role in addressing this imbalance.”

After five years of aiming to improve pay transparency with its annual surveys, The Pay 100 wants RIBA to take ownership of the survey and commit resources to it, developing it into an industry-wide initiative.

“We believe that improving pay transparency across UK architecture should be a core responsibility of the profession’s leading membership body,” said The Pay 100.

“Under the RIBA’s stewardship, the survey could benefit from significantly greater reach, sustained institutional support and broader participation across the profession,” it continued.

“This would provide a foundation for more comprehensive salary data, stronger engagement between employers and employees, and meaningful progress towards better financial conditions throughout the industry.”

The Pay 100 ended its letter by asking for a public response from RIBA by 1 December

#9068. What's Love Got to Do With It? The Relationship Cycle Explained

Relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

Each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

From those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:

Welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

Research shows that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

If the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of new love into a warm, enduring attachment.

Hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the issues head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

Significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

If you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

You know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024

No it's not a flashback to 2024, Epic Games has made its huge Quixel Megascans library free again, and this time it seems it's permanent. Access to the collection of photogrammetry-based 2D and 3D real-world assets was made free for a limited time two years ago to mark the launch of the Fab marketplace, but now it will be free indefinitely.

Quixel features thousands of production-ready items, including 3D models, tileable physically based rendering (PBR) surfaces, vegetation, decals, and custom materials, created by scanning real-world objects, environments. That makes it a massive resource for game developers, 3D artists, VFX artists and those working in architectural visualisation (also see our guides to the best laptops for CAD and the best laptops for 3D modelling).

The full Quixel Megascans library is going free. Fab listings will update between now & Nov 12, so check back if an asset you want isn’t free yet. We’ve updated terms for all Quixel assets so you can train AI models on Megascans & Megaplants. Learn more: https://t.co/jX1C4jRauw https://t.co/nuMDVwvJwcNovember 5, 2026

Megascans currently contains around 23,000 3D scanned assets. Quixel says listings on the Fab marketplace will be updated up until November 12 to make items free. It's also updated the terms for Quixel assets to allow Megascans and Megaplants assets to be used to train AI models.

"Your AI models can now learn from real-world scans to help you generate varied, photorealistic environments for your projects," it says.

Anyone who bought a Megascans or a Quixel Bundle on or after January 1, 2025 should receive a refund to their Epic Account Balance by the end of the year while keeping their licence and getting the new AI rights. The balance can be used across Epic's products, not just on Fab.

Epic has worked to make the new Fab marketplace as easy to use as possible; Channels can be used to discover compatible game engines while a mix of licences ensure you can find the right asset to meet your needs. Fab offers a Creative Commons licence and the Personal or Professional tier of a Standard License. Epic Games press release clarifies: "The Fab Standard License enables you to use the assets, including Megascans, in any game engine or tool you want."

#9066. maison margiela celebrates tokyo flagship anniversary with toothpick-drawn manga

an abandoned electronics factory, strange signals, and a group of researchers set the scene for the factory at night, an illustrated story that explores transformation without erasing the past.

A former electronics factory, strange signals, and a group of researchers investigating an abandoned building set the scene for The Factory at Night, an original manga commissioned by Maison Margiela for the 20th anniversary of its Tokyo flagship in Ebisu. Created by Tokyo-based artist Takehito Moriizumi, the science-fiction story translates the history of the building into an illustrated narrative, with an unusual detail defining its visual identity: the manga is drawn using a toothpick. The limited-edition zine brings together illustration, architecture, fashion, and storytelling, extending the anniversary celebrations of the house.

The narrative begins when a group of electrical engineering researchers visits an abandoned electronics factory to investigate strange signals recently detected inside. As they move through the building, they encounter an environment that seems to hold traces of its former life. Machinery, exposed wiring, industrial structures, staircases, and fragments of everyday objects populate the pages. Their investigation eventually leads to a transformation that introduces something entirely new without completely erasing what existed before.

The visual language of the manga is built around detailed black-and-white illustrations. Architectural elements often dominate the compositions, with complicated structural frameworks, overlapping staircases, suspended platforms, and exposed technical infrastructure creating a dense environment around the characters. The factory feels almost like a character in its own right, its architecture providing both the atmosphere and the narrative framework for the researchers’ investigation.

Moriizumi moves between expansive architectural scenes and more intimate manga panels, introducing the people who inhabit this unusual environment. The illustrations bring fashion into the fictional world through mannequins, garments, and references to the history of the house. The decision to work with a toothpick adds an unexpected material dimension to the publication. At a time when digital illustration, generative imagery, and increasingly automated creative processes are becoming part of visual production, the choice of an unconventional drawing tool invites a closer look at the act of making.

The Maison Margiela Tokyo store occupies a former electrical control equipment manufacturing factory at 2-8-13 Ebisu Minami, a building the house took over in 2006. Its history began six years earlier, when Martin Margiela selected a 1940s traditional Japanese residence in the same neighborhood for the brand’s first-ever retail store. The original boutique opened in September 2000, in an unexpected location away from Tokyo’s established luxury shopping districts of Ginza and Omotesando. The choice reflected the designer’s longstanding relationship with Japan, a country he and the Antwerp Six had regularly visited throughout the 1980s and 1990s.

The house was transformed through one of the Maison’s most recognizable design gestures: Bianchetto, the practice of painting objects and surfaces white. Furniture, architectural elements, and even the property’s tree stumps were covered in white paint, while the original bathroom and shared spaces were retained. When the store had to relocate in 2006, Maison Margiela chose another unconventional building just a five-minute walk away. The former factory offered a different setting, but the approach remained consistent, with the house incorporating elements of its industrial history into the new retail environment rather than erasing its previous function.

The original industrial goods elevator became fitting rooms, a shipping container housed the men’s collection, and a corridor leading to the shoes was constructed entirely from used shoeboxes. Furniture, doors, and display cases salvaged from flea markets and shops across Europe were brought to Tokyo. Parts of the original residential boutique, including its old family bathroom, were also reconstructed inside the new location, creating a physical connection between the two buildings.

Published as part of MaisonMargiela/folders, the manga forms one part of a broader initiative documenting the house’s history, creative identity, and relationship with its surroundings. The first volume of The Factory at Night is released on November 5, 2026, as a limited-edition zine available at selected newsstands across Ebisu and at the Maison Margiela Tokyo store. A digital edition is also being made available internationally through Dropbox.

#9065. Brick bathhouse by Kengo Kuma nears completion in Copenhagen

Pyramidal towers frame pools at the Kai Water Culture House by Japanese studio Kengo Kuma & Associates, which is nearing completion in Copenhagen.

Set to open on the city’s harbour in December, the 5,800-square-metre aquatic centre will contain ten indoor and outdoor pools, alongside wellness facilities and cultural spaces.

Kengo Kuma & Associates was commissioned alongside Danish firms Cornelius Vöge, Søren Jensen and Vilhelm Lauritzen Architects to realise the new cultural and recreational facility on the city’s artificial island of Christiansholm – known locally as Papirøen, or Paper Island.

Photos revealed ahead of the opening show the facility’s five staggered buildings perched atop a glazed base and fronted by a wooden pier that provides direct access to the sea.

“The Water Culture House is a significant new landmark on Copenhagen’s waterfront,” Kengo Kuma & Associates lead architect Yuki Ikeguchi said. “It is part of the story of the city and the harbour’s transformation from an industrial to a cultural harbour.”

“As the cultural cornerstone of Papirøen, the house is a gathering place with water and community as its focal point, embraced by a public harbour bath,” Ikeguchi added.

Constructed from 300,000 handmade bricks, the tapered volumes are punctuated by triangular and square openings that filter dappled light into the indoor pools.

“The bricks are arranged in a staggered, stepped pattern, giving the building its distinctive texture and sculptural character,” Vilhelm Lauritzen Architects said.

“A total of 403 windows of varying sizes act as viewing apertures, framing the surroundings and creating captivating experiences of natural light as it shifts throughout the day,” it added.

The tallest of the five volumes, dubbed the Culture Tower, houses the centre’s cultural programmes, which include a third-floor events space. Meanwhile, the other four towers each house lofty indoor pools.

Nestled between the five brick volumes on the first floor is an outdoor pool, framed by the building’s sloped facades, and an open-air Onsen – a Japanese-style hot spring – that overlooks the harbour.

The Kai Water Culture House is set to open to the public on 5 December, with its wooden pier slated for completion early next year.

The facility sits among a wider redevelopment of Copenhagen’s Paper Island led by Danish studio COBE. Recent projects on the island include a 20,000-square-metre apartment complex informed by the area’s 300-year-old warehouses.

#9064. Vibration Plate Benefits, According to a Weightlifting Coach

Vibration plates are like mini surfboards that give you a good shimmy while you’re exercising. Though you won’t find a mountain of extensive research behind them, you may be impressed by their possible benefits.

We asked a weightlifting coach to explain and show us how to add good vibrations to our workout routine.

These machines, which look like platforms or scales, are designed to activate something called whole-body vibration (WBV). WBV makes the body work harder by forcing it to contract muscles automatically.

Fans of WBV like to perform classic exercises on top of these machines, including:

Research points to WBV’s ability to boost blood flow.

Weightlifting coach Jarrod Nobbe explains that vibration plates help move blood by stimulating muscle contractions through rapid vibrations.

“The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles help pump blood more efficiently throughout the body,” he says.

As Nobbe adds, movement generally increases blood flow and core temperature, preparing the body for activity. This means vibration plates may be an excellent warm-up activity.

A 2021 study showed that WBV can be an alternative exercise for older adults, boosting the effects of strengthening exercise.

Nobbe says this is because WBV engages muscles in a way that mimics resistance training.

“The vibrations activate and force muscles to contract and relax multiple times per second, which can lead to gains in muscle strength and endurance over time, especially when combined with specific exercises,” he says.

Nobbe points to some anecdotal evidence suggesting that regular use of vibration plates may help boost energy levels, possibly thanks to increased blood circulation and enhanced muscle activation.

“Ultimately, I stand by the idea that movement is medicine,” Nobbe says. “Tons of research already proves that regular physical activity boosts mood, mental health, and promotes energy levels.”

Nobbe says WBV may reduce muscle soreness, stiffness, and inflammation by encouraging blood flow to the muscles. This, he explains, aids in faster recovery post-exercise or injury.

WBV has been shown to improve bone mineral density, which Nobbe points out may positively affect those at risk of osteoporosis.

“The mechanical vibrations stimulate bone cells, potentially leading to increased bone density and strength, delivering the same positive bone health benefits of resistance training,” he says.

“Unfortunately, vibration plates aren’t a one-stop shop for weight loss,” Nobbe says.

He explains that vibration plates alone are unlikely to significantly reduce belly fat without dietary changes and additional exercise.

“While vibration plates can contribute to overall calorie expenditure and muscle activation, targeted fat loss requires a comprehensive approach including diet, cardio exercise, and resistance training,” he says.

These tips will help you stand on your vibration plate with a slight bend at your knee or perform exercises on top of it.

More research is needed around WBV — AKA what happens when you use a vibration plate — but existing smaller research is promising.

Use your machine carefully, and remember to maintain a healthy lifestyle and workout routine.

Feeling frustrated on a Monday morning is not a reason to quit. But persistent patterns that affect your health, relationships, and long-term career growth are legitimate signals worth examining. The challenge is separating temporary frustration from genuine misalignment.

The FI community approaches this differently from mainstream career advice. Instead of asking "Am I happy at work?" — which fluctuates daily — we ask: "Is this role aligned with my long-term financial and personal goals?" That reframe turns an emotional decision into a strategic one.

Before you submit your resignation, your finances need to be ready regardless of how miserable you are. Quitting without financial preparation trades one source of stress for another.

The FI community has a massive advantage here. If you have been building toward financial independence — even if you are not there yet — your savings provide a runway that most people do not have. A $200,000 investment portfolio at a 4% safe withdrawal rate provides $8,000 per year in sustainable income, which dramatically reduces the pressure of a job search.

The worst time to make a career decision is when you are emotionally overwhelmed. A terrible meeting, a passed-over promotion, or a toxic interaction with a coworker can make quitting feel urgent when the situation may actually be temporary or fixable.

Use the 30-day test: if you have wanted to quit for fewer than 30 consecutive days, it is likely a temporary frustration. If the feeling has persisted — or intensified — for 30+ days, it is a pattern worth taking seriously.

How you leave a job matters as much as why you leave. Your professional reputation follows you for your entire career, and the people you work with today may be the hiring managers, clients, or references of tomorrow.

Two weeks notice: This is the minimum professional standard in the United States. For senior roles, three to four weeks is more appropriate. Check your employment contract — some roles require 30, 60, or 90 days notice.

The resignation conversation: Schedule a private meeting with your direct manager. Keep it brief and positive. Say: "I have decided to move on to a new opportunity. I want to thank you for [specific positive thing], and I am committed to making the transition as smooth as possible. My last day would be [date]."

The transition plan: Document your ongoing projects, key contacts, passwords, and processes. Offer to train your replacement. Complete as much outstanding work as possible. A strong exit creates goodwill that pays dividends for years.

What not to do: Do not badmouth the company, your boss, or your coworkers — not in the resignation meeting, not in your exit interview, not on social media. Even if your grievances are legitimate, airing them publicly hurts your reputation more than theirs.

Conventional advice says never quit without another job lined up. The FI community takes a more nuanced view: it depends on your financial position and the severity of the situation.

If you are leaving due to company changes — layoffs, restructuring, or role elimination — negotiate your severance package. Many employees accept the first offer without realizing severance is negotiable. Key leverage points include your tenure, difficulty of replacement, willingness to sign a non-compete or non-disparagement clause, and any outstanding commissions or bonuses.

Common severance components to negotiate: extended pay (push for 2-4 weeks per year of tenure), continued health insurance coverage, outplacement services, vesting acceleration for equity, and a positive reference commitment.

Health insurance is often the biggest financial concern when leaving a job. You have two primary options:

COBRA: Continues your employer plan for up to 18 months. You pay the full premium (your share plus what your employer was paying) plus a 2% administrative fee. COBRA typically costs $500-$700 per month for individual coverage and $1,400-$2,000+ for family coverage. It is expensive but familiar.

ACA Marketplace: Depending on your income after leaving, you may qualify for substantial subsidies. If your annual income drops below 400% of the federal poverty level, premium tax credits can reduce your monthly cost to $100-$400 for comprehensive coverage. FI seekers who leave jobs often qualify for significant subsidies because their earned income drops even if their net worth is high — ACA subsidies are based on income, not wealth.

Here is where financial independence changes everything. When you have significant savings — even if you have not reached full FI — you have leverage that most employees lack. You can negotiate from strength, take career risks, and walk away from toxic situations without financial desperation.

A $500,000 portfolio at a 4% withdrawal rate provides $20,000 per year indefinitely. That is not enough to live on for most people, but combined with a working spouse, reduced expenses, or part-time work, it transforms "should I quit my job" from a terrifying question into a strategic calculation. FI is not just about never working again — it is about having the financial security to make career decisions based on alignment and purpose rather than desperation and fear.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

The FI community has a saying: financial independence is not about quitting your job — it is about having the freedom to choose whether to keep it. Every dollar you save and invest is a vote for your future autonomy. When you have 12-24 months of expenses saved, you negotiate from strength. When you reach Coast FI or beyond, a bad job becomes a choice, not a trap. Build your FI runway and the question changes from "Can I afford to quit?" to "Does this role still serve my goals?"

Work through these steps before making your decision.

Have you consistently wanted to leave for 30+ days? If no, wait. Temporary frustration is not a reason to upend your career. If yes, proceed to step two.

Pro tip: Keep a brief daily journal noting your satisfaction level 1-10. Data beats feelings for decision-making.

Is the issue your boss, your role, your compensation, the culture, or the industry? Some problems follow you to the next job. A bad manager is fixable by transferring. An industry you hate requires a bigger change.

Verify your emergency fund, health insurance options, debt situation, and FI runway. If you are not financially ready, keep working while you build your safety net and search for alternatives.

Before quitting, have you requested a transfer, a raise, a role change, or a conversation with HR? Many solvable problems go unaddressed because employees assume the answer will be no.

Pro tip: A direct conversation with your manager about your concerns resolves the issue 40% of the time.

If you decide to leave, secure your next opportunity (if possible), give appropriate notice, document your work for your successor, and maintain every professional relationship.

Pro tip: Never burn bridges. The colleague you leave today may be the hiring manager at your dream company in three years.

At minimum, 3-6 months of essential expenses in a liquid savings account. If you are quitting without another job lined up, aim for 6-12 months. The FI community recommends having your emergency fund fully funded, health insurance secured, and ideally some progress toward financial independence to provide a psychological safety net.

If your job is causing persistent anxiety, depression, or physical health symptoms that do not improve with coping strategies, therapy, or workplace changes — yes, your health must come first. But do it strategically: secure health insurance, build your financial runway, and consult a therapist or career coach before making the leap. Never make a permanent career decision during a temporary emotional crisis.

Generally, quitting gives you more control over the narrative, timing, and terms. Being fired can qualify you for unemployment benefits (quitting usually does not), but it can also create a negative reference. If you sense a termination is coming, consider whether negotiating a mutual separation with severance is an option. Document everything and consult an employment attorney if you believe the termination may be discriminatory or retaliatory.

Be honest and frame it positively. Acceptable explanations include: career transition (took time to retrain or earn a certification), personal development (traveled, volunteered, or cared for family), or strategic job search (took time to find the right fit rather than settling). Employers increasingly accept career gaps — especially post-2020 — as long as you can articulate what you did during the time off.

COBRA (Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act) lets you continue your employer health plan for up to 18 months after leaving. You pay the full premium (your share plus what your employer contributed) plus a 2% admin fee. Individual coverage typically costs $500-$700/month and family coverage runs $1,400-$2,000+/month. The ACA marketplace is often cheaper, especially if your income drops after leaving.

FI savings transform the equation entirely. With a substantial portfolio, you have a financial runway that removes the urgency and desperation from the decision. Even partial FI — having 2-5 years of expenses invested — means you can quit a toxic job, take time to find the right next role, or transition to lower-paying but more fulfilling work. FI is not just about retiring early; it is about having the leverage to make career decisions from a position of strength rather than fear.

The question "should I quit my job?" deserves a framework, not an impulse. Apply the 30-day test, diagnose the real problem, verify your financial readiness, explore internal solutions, and then make a deliberate decision. If you have been building toward financial independence, your savings give you something most people lack: the freedom to walk away from a bad situation without financial panic. FI is the ultimate career insurance — it turns "I have to stay" into "I choose to stay or go." Build your runway, protect your reputation, and make the decision from a position of strength.

#9062. Jaguar designs Knightsbridge flagship to be "physical expression" of Type 01 electric car

Photography courtesy of Jaguar Land Rover

British car brand Jaguar has redesigned its flagship store in Knightsbridge, London, which is the only place in the world where the public can see the recently unveiled Type 01 electric car.

Jaguar overhauled itp show in central London to align its aesthetic with its latest electric car, which was created as the first car in a new era for the brand. It aimed for the flagship store to be a clear departure from the traditional car showroom.

“[We wanted] to create a physical expression of the new Jaguar,” said Jaguar Land Rover spatial brand design team senior manager Nick Rolls, whose team was responsible for overhauling the store.

“Rather than a traditional showroom, we wanted to design a destination where architecture, culture, hospitality and craftsmanship come together – and London felt like a natural home for that vision,” he continued.

“The space has been purpose-designed from the ground up to embody the brand’s new identity – it gave us the opportunity to truly rethink what a Jaguar destination could be outside traditional conventions.”

The showroom has space for two cars to be displayed, one of which is currently the Type 01, with the showroom being the only place in the world where it is on display to the public.

However, the majority of the ground floor of the space is occupied by a restaurant.

Named Café Eighty-One, the restaurant by Michelin-starred chef Michael O’Hare was finished in rich red fabric.

Upholstered benches run around the space, while a series of booths line the front facade of the showroom.

“Food is one of the most universal forms of connection,” said Rolls. “We wanted Café Eighty-One to be a welcoming space where people could spend time, meet friends or discover something new.

“It’s designed to be a destination in its own right, helping make Jaguar at Knightsbridge part of London’s cultural and hospitality landscape,” he continued.

According to Rolls, the extensive use of red was a nod to the surrounding brick architecture in central London.

“Jaguar’s design philosophy is exuberant modernism, so colour plays an important role in creating emotion, atmosphere and a sense of occasion,” he said.

“The rich reds within Café Eighty-One were inspired by London’s iconic red-brick architecture, which is so prevalent throughout Knightsbridge and the surrounding neighbourhoods,” he continued. “It was a way of connecting the interior to its setting while creating a warm, vibrant environment that feels distinctly London.”

Through the rest of the spaces, the materials and colours were chosen to directly evoke the interiors of the Type 01 electric car.

“The relationship is deliberate,” said Rolls. “The interiors share the same emphasis on materiality, craftsmanship and bold, contemporary form that defines Type 01.”

“Materials such as travertine, tactile textiles and warm brass reference the vehicle’s interior, while the use of sculptural shapes, carefully composed lighting and strong geometric forms reflects the same creative philosophy behind the car,” he continued.

While the public restaurant and showroom space are on the ground floor, a lower level contains more private spaces for sales, meetings and for discussions about customisation.

One of these, called the Design Vault, was entirely finished in rich navy blues.

Overall, Rolls hopes that the revamped space will help people understand the current, major rethink that the brand is embarking on.

“I hope people leave with a deeper understanding of Jaguar,” he concluded.

“Every element of the destination has been designed to reflect craftsmanship, creativity and bold design. We want people to feel a genuine connection to the brand and to see Jaguar through a new lens.”

The creation of the showroom follows the launch of Jaguar’s second electric car earlier this year, the Type 01. The car is the production version of the much-discussed Type 00 concept car, which drew much attention in 2024 when it was unveiled following a rebrand for the car company, which was described as a “complete reset”.

#9061. Toot Toot! 6 Tips to Prevent Protein Farts

Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets. They happen because of how proteins are digested. But(t) don’t worry! We have some tips to help you say goodbye to those pungent protein toots without giving up your gains.

Protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant! They’re generally due to upping your protein intake from supplements like protein shakes.

And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.

Farts consist of different gases. The most stinky odors usually come from your gut bacteria, producing sulfur-containing compounds as they break down food. The main culprit is hydrogen sulfide, which gives off a characteristic rotten egg smell, yum!

But why do your protein choices lead to thunder from down under?

Well, there’s not much evidence that a high-protein diet causes protein farts. However, there’s some anecdotal evidence that supplementary protein — like protein bars, protein shakes, and powder powders — increases flatulence, but it’s likely due to non-protein ingredients like lactose.

Supplements containing whey protein or casein are derived from milk and are high in lactose, which can increase flatulence. If your body can’t properly digest lactose, it ends up in your colon, where bacteria feast on it, producing — you guessed it — more gas and cheek flapping.

So, whey protein can throw a curveball for those who are lactose intolerant or sensitive. Surprisingly, it might also stir up digestive drama even for folks who typically handle dairy like champs, potentially due to additives like fart-inducing sweeteners or thickeners.

Some people may also have more significant issues digesting protein. Proteins are big, complex molecules — breaking them down is no small task for your gut. Plant-based protein supplements, like those based on soya beans, may also worsen flatulence.

FYI: Another reason why flatulence is common with protein powders and supplements is due to the addition of artificial sweeteners in the powders and bars, like sugar alcohols, sucralose, sorbitol, xylitol, and stevia.

If you’re looking to continue your protein regimen without becoming a walking, talking whoopee cushion, here are some strategic adjustments you can make:

Don’t just dive into the deep end with your protein intake — wade in slowly. Gradually increasing the amount of protein you consume allows your digestive system to adjust without getting overwhelmed. This step-by-step approach can help minimize the likelihood of excessive gas.

Keep the water flowing. Drinking plenty of water is crucial as it helps your digestive system handle higher protein levels more efficiently. Proper hydration aids in the breakdown and absorption of nutrients, which can help prevent gas buildup.

Sometimes, your body needs a little extra help. Enzyme supplements like Beano or Lactaid can be game-changers, especially if you consume proteins that your body struggles with. These supplements help break down proteins and lactose, making digestion smoother and less gassy.

Variety isn’t just the spice of life — it can also be the solution to your protein fart problems. If whey protein tends to upset your stomach, explore other options like plant-based or animal-based proteins that might be easier to digest. Diversifying your protein sources can also ensure you get a broad range of nutrients.

What you blend your protein powder with can make a big difference. If you’re whipping up a protein shake, be mindful of adding high-fiber fruits and vegetables, as these can also increase gas production. Try to find a balance that allows you to enjoy the benefits of protein and fiber without the extra flatulence.

Introducing probiotics into your diet can improve your gut health, which can help manage and reduce gas production. Whether through supplements or probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, or sauerkraut, boosting your gut flora can aid in better overall digestion and less discomfort from gas.

Protein farts are a rather windy side effect of a high-protein diet, but they don’t have to knock you off course. Try easing into your protein consumption, staying hydrated, diversifying your protein sources, and integrating enzyme supplements or probiotics to max those gains, minus the stink bombs!

Last medically reviewed on June 30, 2024

#9060. SCI-Arc task force champions long-term architectural strategies for fire-prone areas

the sci-arc resilient futures task force supports los angeles homeowners recovering from the 2025 wildfires, offering climate-resilient architectural solutions to replace outdated building habits.

The SCI-Arc Resilient Futures Task Force was created to rethink standard rebuilding methods after the January 2025 fires in Los Angeles exposed deep weaknesses in Southern California’s default residential. Bringing together teachers, researchers, and students, the initiative gives displaced homeowners direct, practical help with building safety, soil toxicity, emergency funding, and insurance claims through public community meetings.

Nearly two years later, residents are still rebuilding their lives as wildfires become more frequent and severe. Instead of repeating past mistakes caused by outdated safety codes, standard construction habits, and insurance gaps, this crisis presents a critical moment to create safer, long-term architectural designs in fire-prone areas.

Grounded in the institution’s tradition of critical design research, the Resilient Futures Task Force connects academic expertise directly with real-world disaster recovery. The coalition brings together an international network of architects, structural engineers, scientists, material specialists, non-profit developers, and financial strategists. Key collaborators and participating institutions include Code Red Consultants, Angel City Lumber, SGH, JPMorgan Chase, Century Housing, Clearinghouse CDFI, Builders FirstSource, Plant Prefab, Sexsmith Architects, Timberlab, ReSAWN, Urban Machine, and TU Delft.

Extending its focus from temporary aid to permanent resilience, the Task Force organized public panels on alternative building materials, mass timber construction, rebuilding economics, and fire-adapted landscaping to help communities make informed, long-term architectural decisions.

The initiative’s first year concluded with Architecture After the Fires, a landmark public exhibition showcasing nearly 70 speculative and actionable home design proposals tailored for fire zones. As the largest collection of Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) architectural proposals to date, the showcase featured ongoing work from prominent practices including Lorcan O’Herlihy, SPF:architects, Studio Murnane, Morphosis, Heather Flood and Story Dimson Studio, Knowhow Shop, and Scott Uriu.

The Task Force is publishing a comprehensive book documenting these projects, creating a permanent reference guide for building in high-risk environments. Next, SCI-Arc plans to expand its research through institutional partnerships that combine artificial intelligence, environmental risk modeling, and advanced simulation to shape resilient building standards across the region.

#9059. Arches create “animated silhouette” at red-brick apartment block in King’s Cross

Two-storey-tall arches frame entrances to Cadence, a mixed-use apartment block in King’s Cross, London, which has been completed by local studio Alison Brooks Architects.

Positioned at the northern end of Lewis Cubitt Park, the prominent red-brick building combines 163 apartments alongside commercial and social spaces organised around an open-air courtyard.

Signposted by its two towers, the building by Alison Brooks Architects forms part of the wider King’s Cross redevelopment and is complete with views overlooking Heatherwick Studios’ Coal Drops Yard to the south.

According to studio founder Alison Brooks, the building’s red-brick exterior was chosen to pay homage to the nearby St Pancras Station, while its arched openings draw on the area’s neo-gothic architecture and were conceived as a “civic welcoming gesture”.

“The main concept of the project was to make a clear statement of welcome and arrival in King’s Cross, but from the north end of the master plan rather than the south end, which everybody is familiar with,” Brooks told Dezeen.

“My first instinct was to respond to King’s Cross’ iconic railway station architecture, sculpting the site massing to create an animated silhouette. A language of two-story high arches creates a really generous, welcoming gesture at street level and toward the park,” she added.

The building is formed of a five-sided block, with no designated front or back, which rises to form two towers reaching 12 and 16 storeys respectively.

For its construction, the studio opted for a Design for Manufacture and Assembly approach, which saw 85 per cent of the building’s components prefabricated off-site.

At the centre of its angular plan, an open-air courtyard, complete with a reflecting pool, has been wrapped by sheltered walkways that provide a shared circulation space between the building’s private and commercial programmes.

“It’s a multifaceted building,” Brooks said. “Each facet of the pentagon has a particular identity or address to the space that it’s adjacent to.”

“This idea of making a very connected space at the base of the building, even though it’s a courtyard, is visually trying to connect all the sides of the plot to the city around it.”

“It’s a place of movement and light and also a kind of special quality because of the reflecting pool,” she added.

The building’s first two floors have been dedicated to 633 square metres of commercial and social spaces, which include a “community living room” that opens onto the courtyard at ground level.

A prefabricated lift system connects to the upper floors, where the 163 residential units benefit from both courtyard and street views.

A combination of rectangular and arched windows draws daylight into the building’s white-walled interior, complemented by private balconies and communal roof terraces.

Other projects developed as part of the King’s Cross regeneration include Google’s landscraper office building by architecture studios BIG and Heatherwick and an office block designed by Coffey Architects to recall the area’s industrial spaces.

#9058. Undercuts for Women: Benefits, Styles, and Types

Is it time to give your hairstyle and scalp a breath of fresh air? Say hello to the undercut hairstyle, a fashion-forward solution that can elevate your look and promote skin health.

By significantly reducing hair volume, undercuts allow for improved air circulation around the scalp. The result? Less trapped heat and moisture — factors that can contribute to fungal infections, scalp acne, dandruff, and dermatitis.

Whether you’re battling irritation or want to give your “do” a new lease on life, continue reading to learn how undercut hairstyles can be your ally in style and scalp health.

An undercut involves shaving or cutting hair very short on the sides or back of the head while leaving the hair on top longer.

Originally popular in men’s hairstyling, the undercut has crossed gender boundaries and gained popularity among peeps seeking a hairstyle that stands out.

It’s a style that offers a stark contrast and is often used to add an edge to an otherwise conventional look. So whether it’s a side undercut, undercut pixie, mullet undercut, or nape undercut, these hairstyles for women, men, and folks of all genders enhance individuality while offering practical benefits like reduced drying time and less hair maintenance.

Choosing an undercut means embracing a hairstyle with a “heady” mix of aesthetic and practical benefits. Here’s why an undercut might be the refreshing change you need.

Ready to turn heads? The standout feature of an undercut is undoubtedly its unique appearance. Hidden under the longer layers, it packs a punch of boldness you can flaunt or conceal — whatever fits your vibe. You can control the reveal, whether you’re showcasing that edgy undercut for a night out or keeping it classy for the office.

Got a mane that’s more lioness than laid-back? An undercut might be your new BFF. Strategically shaving or trimming the hair short on the sides or back dramatically dials down the volume. This means your thick, voluminous hair becomes way easier to manage and style, turning a heavy head of hair into something light and breezy.

And the best part? You get to keep all the styling potential without any of the hassle. It’s a practical solution that doesn’t sacrifice style for comfort.

Are you chasing the clock every morning? An undercut could slash your prep time. With less hair to fuss over, you can breeze through your washing, drying, and styling routine faster than you can say “snooze button.”

This trimmed-down approach is a time-saver and reduces the daily wear and tear from blow dryers and straighteners, keeping hair healthier in the long run.

Undercuts reduce your scalp’s weight and improve hair follicle airflow. This keeps the scalp cooler and reduces the buildup of sweat and oil that can lead to scalp irritation, dermatitis, and dandruff. As a result, undercuts could lead to more robust, healthier hair growth.

Ready to shake up your style with a cool undercut? Here’s a rundown of some options to add a dash of daring to your daily look:

Are you looking for a dramatic change without total commitment? Try the side-swept undercut.

This style features a sleek shave on one side of the head, just above the ear, while keeping the hair on top and the other side longer.

It’s perfect for folks who love to play with contrast — sweep the top hair over to the shaved side for an instant bold statement.

If subtlety is more your speed, this undercut is a wicked choice. It’s a shaved area tucked away at the back of the head or underneath the top layer of hair so that it can play a fantastic game of hide-and-seek.

Wear your hair down for a business-as-usual look, or tie it up to reveal a sneaky, stylish surprise. It’s an excellent choice for peeps wanting a touch of edge.

Are you feeling bold and artistic? Design Undercuts take personal expression to the next level. These chic undercuts are masterpieces, boasting intricate geometric patterns, sweet floral motifs, or any design that speaks to you.

Do you prefer a more understated yet stylish look? The tapered undercut starts very short near the ear and gracefully lengthens as it ascends the head, blending with your other locks.

It’s a softer version of the undercut that pairs beautifully with bob or lob cuts and offers a gentle nod to the undercut trend without going full-throttle.

The undercut hair offers both style and substance. It reduces styling time and promotes scalp health. By alleviating the weight and allowing the scalp to breathe, undercuts can help minimize issues like overheating and irritation, especially during warmer months.

Whether you’re drawn to the edgy designs or the subtle tapered style, an undercut could be a clever hack to simplify your morning routine. More time for coffee, less time with the comb!

Last medically reviewed on June 30, 2024

#9057. Neri Oxman experiments with fabric pigment created by bacteria

Designer Neri Oxman has created a fabric dyeing concept where a bacterial solution is sprayed onto a 3D-knitted silk textile and left to grow a living culture producing faded indigo and pink pigments.

The project, called Vigils, was developed by the designer’s studio, Oxman, for designers, artists and collaborators to “create new forms of material and aesthetic expression”.

Tussah silk thread within the fabric is coated with “bacterially sensitive chemicals”, which act as “a bioreactor” once mixed with the spray.

The fabric then sits for 24 hours, during which the solution and chemicals begin to interact and eventually produce a living bacterial culture. This organism, “numbering in the billions of cells”, spreads across the fabric and converts amino acids into the pigments Indigo and Melanin.

For the process, the Oxman lab created a spray solution containing the BL21 strain of Escherichia coli (E. coli), a strain commonly used in biotechnology and synthetic biology research, and sprayed it onto a silk fabric.

Its growth pattern is directed by “where and how densely the designer directed the culture to grow” via the spray, according to the team.

The fabric is then washed and dried, removing the bacteria, but the pigment remains.

“The microorganisms respond to signals associated with the textile substrate, making biological activity an active component of the material process,” said the team. “Vigils is a research-driven exploration of biological textile colouration.”

“The project is intended to investigate the interaction between synthetic biology and material systems rather than to represent a fully optimised industrial dyeing process.”

The studio created a series of four capes to demonstrate the technique. They display the variations in the muted colours and patterns created by the bacteria.

The studio is presenting the process as a possible alternative to “resource-intensive” industrial dyeing processes.

“The result is not simply an alternative way of applying color: the biological process becomes part of the design itself, producing patterns and variations that could not be achieved through conventional dyeing and making each textile an expression of the process that created it,” said Oxman.

It has not undergone extensive Life Cycle Assessment, which measures its environmental outputs, and is still in the prototype stage.

Neri Oxman opened a New York studio in Midtown Manhattan in 2024 and unveiled an AI-designed skyscraper to demonstrate its computational abilities at the time.

The designer is known for her work in material ecology, but she also faced allegations of plagiarism in her PhD thesis completed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

#9056. Hickey Stages: Understanding and Managing Love Bites Effectively

Hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti. If you’ve ever scrambled for scarves or turtlenecks, welcome to the kissing booth of knowledge! Join us as we navigate the lifecycle of hickeys, from their eye-catching start to their subtle fade, and learn how to speed up their departure.

A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck. This intense suction causes the tiny blood vessels under the skin, a.k.a. capillaries, to burst and release blood into the surrounding tissues. The immediate result? An unmistakable red or purple mark that gradually shifts to a darker shade as it heals.

From a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing. They showcase the skin’s sensitivity and the body’s rapid response to minor vascular injury. Not so romantic when you think about it scientifically, right? But hey, it’s all part of the human experience of showing affection — or something like that.

When you get a hickey, your body starts a healing process that resembles how it deals with other bruises. Here’s a more detailed look at each stage of a hickey’s life cycle.

Immediately after the passionate moment, a hickey appears on the skin, screaming in shades of bright red or deep purple. This initial coloration is due to blood from the ruptured capillaries pooling beneath the skin’s surface in response to the suction. It’s your skin’s way of signaling that there’s been some minor internal damage in that area.

As the hickey begins to heal, it undergoes a whole wardrobe of color transformations, showcasing your body’s metabolic process at work.

Initially, the hickey darkens as the blood begins to oxidize. Then, after a few days, the body starts to break down and reabsorb the blood, so it turns lighter — going from blue to green to brown and, finally, mellow yellow. This rainbow journey reflects the breakdown of hemoglobin, the iron-containing substance in the blood, into biliverdin and bilirubin.

Finally, your hickey starts to ghost you. Over a week or two, depending on factors like your skin type, overall health, how severe the hickey was., and how your body rides the healing waves, the last traces of your hickey fade into nothing.

During this stage, the body’s immune system clears away the remaining by-products of the broken-down blood. White blood cells swoop in like a cleanup crew at a festival, gobbling up and digesting the debris in a process called phagocytosis, while increased blood flow to the area helps to flush out the remnants.

Need a hickey gone yesterday? Here’s how to help your hickey heal. Start with a cold pack — grab a spoon from the freezer or a chilled gel pack and gently press it against your hickey. This will help reduce any swelling and scatter the blood pooling under your skin, which can help minimize that bold bruise.

After using cold treatment for the first 48 hours, it’s time to turn up the heat. Switch to warm compresses to get the blood flowing smoothly again. A few minutes a few times a day invites more circulation to the hickey zone, helping you hustle through healing and clear out the blood remnants more swiftly.

You can also try a dab of comfrey ointment. Research shows it may reduce bruise size and coloration for some peeps.

Caught off guard? A little concealer or foundation over the hickey makes it less noticeable.

Not into makeup? Scarves and high-necked shirts are also great accessories for your camouflage arsenal.

Typically, a hickey will last anywhere from 5 days to 2 weeks, depending on its severity and your body’s healing capabilities.

Communication is key! Let your partner know your feelings about receiving a hickey — some might find it fun, while others may prefer to keep their necks clear.

While generally harmless, hickeys can sometimes lead to complications like skin infections or, very rarely, blood clots. It’s best to keep the affection gentle to avoid any issues.

Hickeys are nothing more than bruises in disguise. They start as bright red to purple love stamps and gradually fade over several days to a couple of weeks. Speed up the process with heat and cold packs or a splodge of comfrey cream.

Remember, the best approach to handling hickeys — like all aspects of relationships — is communication and care. So go forth, love responsibly, and keep a scarf handy, just in case!
